meta.description: Resolves GWAS associations to candidate causal variants and credible sets via SuSiE, susie_rss, FINEMAP, CAVIAR, DAP-G, PAINTOR, PolyFun, SuSiEx, MultiSuSiE, and FOCUS. Use when narrowing a GWAS lead SNP to a 95 percent credible set, choosing between in-sample and reference LD, calibrating non-sparse loci, integrating functional priors via PolyFun, fine-mapping across ancestries, diagnosing LD mismatch, handling HLA, or feeding credible sets into coloc.susie.

scientific_integrity.detail: All literature citations (Wang 2020 JRSSB, Zou 2022 PLoS Genet, Cui 2024 Nat Genet, Benner 2016 Bioinformatics, Weissbrod 2020 Nat Genet, Yuan 2024 Nat Genet, etc.) are real and correctly attributed, unchanged from the pre-fix audit; no fabricated statistics anywhere in the fixed Skill.

practice_boundaries.detail: Population-genetics / statistical-genomics research workflow only; no individual diagnostic, prescriptive, or treatment claims anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.

methodological_ground.detail: The 'Credible-set misinterpretation' section still rejects reporting a single top-PIP SNP as causal (re-verified in Input 7); the Neff case-control correction remains correctly stated and empirically confirmed.

code_usability.detail: All 7 executed R/Python code patterns ran cleanly against real planted-truth data or real PolyFun/GWAS output in this round, including the two patterns that previously either crashed (coloc.susie, Input 4) or could not be tested at all (PolyFun integration, Input 8). No open code-usability defect remains.

functional_suitability.note: The one verified correctness gap from the pre-fix audit (coloc.susie example, Input 4) is fixed and regression-confirmed: SKILL.md's own documented code now succeeds on an unmodified first pass. No remaining correctness gap found across 9 inputs.

reliability.note: The coloc.susie SNP-naming precondition is now stated explicitly in prose (a dedicated 'Precondition' paragraph) AND listed in the Common Errors table with the exact cryptic error text to expect. Held at 11/12 rather than 12/12 because the fix is documentation, not a code-level guard (no stopifnot/validation in the worked example itself would catch a user who still skips it).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew from 436 to 444 lines (two new notes: Precondition paragraph, Platform note) with still no references/ folder; unchanged from pre-fix -- the fix log explicitly declined this restructuring as out of the fix's scope.

agent_usability.note: The Common Errors table now includes the coloc.susie data.table-error row, and the new Platform note sits at the top of the Approach block, before any CLI tool's first mention. Both catalogs are now complete for the failure modes this audit exercised.

human_usability.note: The one previously-undocumented error (coloc.susie naming) is now documented in plain language at the point of use; Category-3 forgiveness override still applies (strict input validation is correct here).

security.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: no credentials or sensitive data; explicit PSD/eigenvalue and convergence checks exist for the summary-statistic path; still no code-level pre-flight check for the coloc.susie naming precondition (prose only).

maintainability.note: Unchanged: clean separation across SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/; the Tips-section redundancy pass (usage-guide.md) removed duplication without losing content, re-verified directly in Input 9.

agent_specific.note: The new Platform note is itself a stronger escape hatch (explicitly tells the agent not to attempt FINEMAP/SuSiEx/PAINTOR/DAP-G natively on Windows and names the fallback), raising this from 18 to 19. Progressive Disclosure remains the one weak sub-criterion: still no references/ folder.

inputs.label: PolyFun --compute-h2-L2 -> susie_rss prior_weights, real GWAS + real PolyFun output
inputs.note: NEW input, not in the pre-fix audit (PolyFun was not installed then; scored by inspection only). Ran SKILL.md's exact documented 'polyfun.py --compute-h2-L2 --no-partitions' command against PolyFun's own bundled real GWAS (chr22 RBC subset, N=383,290, 2,511 SNPs) and real baseline-LF-style annotations. Output column is exactly 'SNPVAR' (case-sensitive, as SKILL.md warns). Fed the real per-SNP priors into susie_rss on a 300-SNP window with a planted weak causal effect at the real highest-SNPVAR SNP: uniform-prior PIP=0.8966, real-prior_weights PIP=0.9979 (sharpened, as documented). Also empirically reproduced the Skill's documented 'prior_weights vs prior_variance confusion' failure mode for the first time with real data: passing the same vector to prior_variance ran without error and silently returned the uniform-prior PIP (0.8966) unchanged -- exactly the 'PIPs nearly identical to the uniform-prior fit' symptom SKILL.md describes.

recommendations.title: coloc.susie's SNP-naming precondition is documented but not defensively checked in code
recommendations.problem: The Precondition paragraph and Common Errors row explain the naming requirement in prose, but the worked example itself has no stopifnot()/validation step that would catch a user who still omits it before calling coloc.susie.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix addressed the documentation gap (the actual pre-fix P1) but did not add a code-level guard, which was outside the fix's declared scope.
recommendations.fix: Optionally add `stopifnot(!is.null(names(z1)), !is.null(names(z2)))` immediately before the `coloc.susie()` call in the worked example, so a skipped precondition fails fast with a clear message instead of only being caught by careful reading.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md carries all technical depth inline rather than in a references/ folder
recommendations.problem: At 444 lines (up from 436 pre-fix), SKILL.md loads its full Algorithmic Taxonomy, Quantitative Thresholds, and Anticipated Reviewer Pushback tables every time the Skill triggers, rather than deferring this depth to a conditionally-loaded reference file.
recommendations.root_cause: No references/ directory exists for this Skill; the fix log explicitly declined this restructuring as beyond the fix's scope (redundancy removal only, not new reference extraction).
recommendations.fix: Move the Algorithmic Taxonomy, Quantitative Thresholds, and Anticipated Reviewer Pushback tables into references/fine_mapping_reference.md, leaving SKILL.md as a leaner entry point with a pointer to it.

recommendations.title: Individual-level and CLI code paths still lack an explicit genotype-QC checklist
recommendations.problem: The summary-statistics path has explicit PSD/eigenvalue and convergence checks; the individual-level susie(X,y) path and the CLI examples still have no equivalent guidance on genotype-level quality control (call rate, HWE, MAF floor) before fitting.
recommendations.root_cause: Unchanged from the pre-fix audit; the fix log declined this as new content outside the fix's scope.
recommendations.fix: Add a brief genotype-QC checklist alongside the susie(X, y) pattern and the FINEMAP/SuSiEx prerequisites.
